The current game engine hides missing-item choices; the locked-card behavior is a future integration requirement, not implemented by this review JSON. Preserve hidden story-state conditional choices.

bladderFirstRevision.note: Nate superseded earlier wedding-help approvals: no groom escort or wedding reunion. Boiler Three is a brief source of lavatory directions and optional ring gag. hotel_entry_dispatch.text: You leave the People's Pavilion behind. The next restroom symbol is closer than you expect.

choices.text: CONTINUE
CONTINUE
CONTINUE
CONTINUE
CONTINUE
CONTINUE
CONTINUE

entry_locomotion_fail.text:
The last foam cushion falls off your shoulder.

You stand in the loading lane behind the People's Pavilion. The padded collection cart that deposited you outside is already disappearing through a mechanical doorway.

Across the lane, several workmen are unloading an enormous ornamental staircase from the back of a freight truck.

The staircase appears to be coming out of the building rather than going in.

GRAND BELLEVUE HOTEL, reads the sign above the loading bay.

Beyond the workers, through an open service entrance, you spot a small rectangular sign. RESTROOMS.

You look at the staircase. You look at the sign. You decide the workers probably know what they're doing.

choices.text: CONTINUE

entry_presenter_help_end.text:
You emerge from the Pavilion's maintenance passage into a narrow service alley.

Fresh air. Daylight. No announcer telling you how well you're performing.

A magnificent improvement.

Two men struggle past carrying an enormous upholstered sofa between them. Behind them, a third man pushes a trolley loaded with wedding decorations.

They disappear into the loading entrance of the Grand Bellevue Hotel.

A sign beside the entrance points toward the hotel's service facilities. Below a small restroom symbol, somebody has written STAFF AND VISITORS.

You have never been so grateful to be either.

You follow the workers inside.

choices.text: CONTINUE

entry_paper_problem_end.text:
A strip of receipt paper remains tangled around your shoe.

You pull it free as you cross the courtyard outside the People's Pavilion.

Nearby, a group of wedding guests are entering an extravagant hotel. One woman looks at the ribbon of paper in your hand, smiles, and points approvingly toward the decorations above the entrance.

You look up. GRAND BELLEVUE HOTEL.

Flowers surround the enormous glass doors. Somewhere inside, an orchestra is playing. Beside the entrance is a sign bearing the familiar restroom symbol.

You drop the paper.

For the moment, nobody seems interested in stopping you. You enter the hotel.

choices.text: CONTINUE

entry_attendant_honest_end.text:
The Pavilion's service door closes behind you.

The attendant's parting words stay with you. You hope you find somewhere to go, too.

Across the service yard, a delivery truck reverses toward the Grand Bellevue Hotel. Its driver is arguing with a man carrying an enormous flower arrangement.

The hotel's delivery entrance stands open, held in place by a wooden crate. WEDDING CAKE - THIS SIDE UP.

The crate is lying on its side.

Beyond the entrance, you notice a familiar symbol mounted above a narrow corridor. A restroom.

Perhaps the attendant's good wishes have finally accomplished something. You slip inside.

choices.text: CONTINUE

entry_door_dash_fail.text:
You straighten your coat outside the People's Pavilion.

Your unsuccessful attempt to reach its restroom has apparently provided considerable entertainment for everyone involved.

Across the courtyard, a formally dressed couple hurry toward the entrance of an enormous hotel. The man is carrying a wedding gift. The woman is carrying an expression suggesting the man has done something wrong.

They disappear through the glass doors.

You notice the building's restroom sign. You look back at the Pavilion. You consider the distance between the two buildings.

The hotel seems considerably more promising.

You cross the courtyard and enter.

choices.text: CONTINUE

entry_door_reverse_end.text:
The ridiculous ribbon remains pinned to your coat. FASTEST SATISFIED VISITOR.

You have never felt less satisfied.

As you approach the neighboring hotel, a woman carrying several flower arrangements stops directly in front of you. She reads the ribbon. Her eyes brighten.

She mistakes you for the fast helper she needs and takes your arm. The groom has disappeared, the musicians are arguing, and somebody has taken the chairs.

You attempt to explain that you are not employed by the hotel. She is already guiding you through a side entrance.

A moment later, you find yourself standing in the middle of an elaborate wedding reception. You glance back toward the lobby. The restroom sign is still visible.

Unfortunately, the woman has noticed you looking away.

choices.text: CONTINUE

entry_backstage_exit.text:
You reach the building across the courtyard. GRAND BELLEVUE HOTEL.

Its enormous glass doors open onto a magnificent lobby. Music drifts from an adjoining ballroom. Guests in formal clothing wander between towering flower arrangements and polished furniture.

You barely notice them.

At the far end of the lobby are two doors bearing unmistakable restroom symbols. Actual restroom symbols. On actual restroom doors.

You begin walking.

Then somebody shouts. SOLD! SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY!

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_lobby_view.text:
The hotel's lobby is magnificent. Crystal chandeliers, immense flower arrangements, an orchestra playing somewhere beyond the ballroom doors.

At the far end of the lobby is a pair of restroom doors. You begin walking toward them.

Then someone shouts. SOLD! SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY!

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_auctioneer_arrival.speaker: hotel_auctioneer

text.desc: An elderly gentleman in a crimson dinner jacket stands behind a wooden auction podium. He gestures grandly toward two workmen.

text: SOLD! SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY!
Gentlemen! Kindly assist our fortunate buyer!

text.desc: The workmen approach the restroom entrance. One produces a screwdriver. The other begins removing the hinges.

text.say: Papa!

text: Darling! You look radiant!

text.say: You're selling the bathrooms!

text: The doors, sweetheart. Only the doors.

text.say: You promised the auction wouldn't start until after the wedding!

text: And it hasn't! Not officially. These are merely preliminary sales.

text.desc: A workman lifts the first restroom door off its hinges.

text.say: Papa, you're dismantling the hotel!

text: Don't be dramatic. The hotel is perfectly sound.

text.desc: An enormous metallic crash echoes from upstairs. A moment later, a grand piano rolls past the lobby entrance on a freight trolley.

text: Mostly sound.

text.desc: The bride closes her eyes. You look toward the restroom. The workmen are preparing to remove the second door.

choices.text: WALK STRAIGHT INTO THE RESTROOM WHILE THE WORKMEN REMOVE THE DOORS.
HAVE YOU SOLD ALL THE RESTROOMS, OR IS THERE ONE LEFT?

hotel_service_arrival.text:
The hotel's loading area is enormous. Freight elevators line one wall. Wooden crates occupy another. A collection of expensive furniture stands between them, waiting to be removed.

A mechanical hoist slowly lowers an ornate chandelier into a padded shipping container.

Two workmen argue over a piano that appears to be considerably wider than the doorway through which they intend to move it.

A third man, wearing rolled-up sleeves and a battered cap, watches the proceedings with mounting irritation. He notices you.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_service_foreman.speaker: hotel_salvage_foreman
text: You! Stay clear of that lift!

text.desc: He points toward the piano.

text: If that thing tips over, I'm not putting it back together.

text.desc: A tremendous crash comes from somewhere upstairs. The foreman closes his eyes.

text: That's another one.
You collecting something?

text.desc: You point toward the staff facilities corridor.

text: Lavatory's down there. Unless they've sold that too.

text.desc: He turns back to the freight equipment. For once, nobody asks you to help move anything.

choices.text: FOLLOW THE RESTROOM SIGN THROUGH THE SERVICE CORRIDOR.
TAKE THE FREIGHT ELEVATOR UP TO THE BALLROOM.

hotel_wedding_arrival.speaker: hotel_wedding_organizer

text.desc: The organizer releases your arm in the lavishly decorated reception hall. Musicians argue beside a piano while workmen carry furniture through a side door.

text: Now, listen carefully.

text.desc: You interrupt by pointing toward the nearest restroom symbol. The organizer follows your gesture.

text: There's a private lavatory off the bridal dressing room. I have the key, but—

text.desc: A crash comes from the ballroom. She winces.

text: Give me one moment.

choices.text: I NEED THAT PRIVATE LAVATORY. CAN YOU OPEN THE DRESSING ROOM?
SLIP THROUGH THE SERVICE DOOR WHILE THE ORGANIZER IS DISTRACTED.

hotel_restroom_entry.text:
You walk directly between the workmen carrying away the restroom doors. Neither attempts to stop you. One even steps aside politely.

You enter. The bathroom is immaculate. Polished tiles. Clean sinks. Fresh towels.

Three private stalls stand against the far wall. And there, visible through the open door of the nearest stall, is an actual porcelain toilet.

You stare at it. It has a seat. It has a tank. It has plumbing. There isn't even a sign explaining that you've already used it.

You take a step forward. A workman kneeling beneath one of the sinks looks up.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_restroom_plumber.speaker: hotel_plumber
text: Oh! Sorry, sir.

text.desc: He sets down his wrench.

text: Didn't know anybody was still using the facilities. Go right ahead. I'll give you a minute.

text.desc: You are almost overcome by gratitude. The plumber turns toward his assistant, who is disconnecting a copper pipe.

text: Hold off on that one, Eddie. Gentleman needs the lavatory.

text.say: Right you are!

text.desc: A metallic snapping sound comes from beneath the sink. The plumber's expression changes.

text: Eddie?

text.desc: A violent jet of water erupts from the wall, strikes the opposite sink, ricochets across the floor, and sends fresh towels flying. You jump backward. The plumber lunges toward a valve and finds only a bare metal shaft.

text: Oh, for the love of—

text.say: What's wrong?

text: Where's the bloody shutoff wheel?

text.say: Sold it.

text.desc: The plumber closes his eyes.

text: Of course you did.

text.say: Fella gave twelve for it. Said it looked nautical.

text: It's a valve handle, Eddie!

text.say: Well, he didn't ask.

text.desc: A second pipe begins rattling. The plumber looks at it.

text: Terribly sorry, sir. Little trouble with the plumbing. Possibly a medium-sized trouble.

text.desc: Above the sinks hangs a locked cabinet marked EMERGENCY WATER ISOLATION. Its brass keyhole appears to be one of the few fittings nobody has bought.

choices.text: HELP THE PLUMBER TURN THE BARE VALVE SHAFT BEFORE ANOTHER PIPE BURSTS.

pass.result: You catch the bare spindle between the wrench's jaws. It shudders, then turns. The violent spray collapses to a thin, furious dribble.

fail.result: The wrench slips. A dreadful metallic pop comes from inside the wall. The spray doubles and knocks you into a stack of clean towels.

choices.text: FOLLOW THE PLUMBING THROUGH THE MAINTENANCE ACCESS.
WHO BOUGHT THE SHUTOFF WHEEL?

wc_key.say: TRY THE FACILITIES KEY IN THE EMERGENCY CABINET.

wip_auctioneer_question.text: DRAFT REVIEW STOP — A2 auctioneer conversation and auction incidents not yet written. This is not a gameplay ending.

wip_freight_lift.text: DRAFT REVIEW STOP — S3 freight lift route not yet written. This is not a gameplay ending.

wip_wedding_service.text: DRAFT REVIEW STOP — W2 wedding service route not yet written. This is not a gameplay ending.

hotel_valve_braced.text:
The plumber throws his weight against the wrench and holds the shaft in place. Water drips from his sleeves. He warns you that the seal is temporary. Nobody should touch a tap, and absolutely nobody should flush.

You look at the nearest toilet. It is still the most beautiful thing you have seen all day.

From the hall comes the scrape of a freight trolley. Two porters stop outside the open restroom entrance. One consults a card.

LOT FIFTY-THREE. THREE COMPLETE STALLS.

The plumber stares at the ceiling. You have apparently bought everyone a minute, which he strongly recommends spending somewhere else.

choices.text: TRY TO REACH A STALL BEFORE THE PORTERS TAKE IT.
LEAVE THE PLUMBER HOLDING THE VALVE AND TAKE THE SERVICE ACCESS.

hotel_valve_flood.text:
For a moment there is nothing but water.

Then Eddie floats past on an overturned basket of clean towels, looking astonished by the speed at which his employment has deteriorated.

The plumber catches a sink with one hand. The other points toward a small service panel hanging open behind you. He shouts for you to get through it.

Water pours beneath the missing restroom doors and races down the hotel corridor. Somewhere beyond it, a woman screams about her wedding dress. The water seems to be winning.

choices.text: SCRAMBLE THROUGH THE OPEN MAINTENANCE PANEL.
FOLLOW THE FLOOD INTO THE WEDDING CORRIDOR.

hotel_pipe_tunnel.text:
You duck through the access panel behind the sinks. The space beyond is wider than expected: a narrow maintenance walkway with pipes along one wall and hotel rooms on the other.

A brass plate reads CENTRAL WATER ISOLATION — STAFF ONLY. Someone has hung a numbered auction tag from it.

Farther along the walkway, a man in a wedding suit is crouched behind a boiler. His boutonnière is caught on a bolt. He sees you and immediately puts a finger to his lips.

At the opposite end, an EXIT TO LOADING DOCK sign points down a steep iron stairway.

You have found three things. None is a toilet.

choices.text: ASK THE MAN IN WEDDING CLOTHES WHAT HE IS HIDING FROM.
INSPECT THE HOTEL'S CENTRAL WATER CONTROLS.
TAKE THE IRON STAIRS TOWARD THE LOADING DOCK.

hotel_isolator_panel.text:
Two great brass levers stand inside a recessed metal frame.

RESTROOMS, reads the neat engraved label beneath the first.

ENTIRE HOTEL, reads the label beneath the second.

Someone has pasted a fresh auction sticker across the frame: LOT NINETEEN — TWO MATCHING DECORATIVE LEVERS.

From the restroom wall comes the unmistakable sound of water hitting something it should not. Both levers appear to be connected.

choices.text: SHUT OFF WATER TO THE RESTROOMS ONLY.
CLOSE THE MAIN WATER SUPPLY FOR THE ENTIRE HOTEL.

hotel_isolator_restrooms.text:
The RESTROOMS lever moves with a satisfying clunk. The hiss in the pipes fades. A moment later, through the wall, you hear the plumber give a grateful cheer.

You retrace your steps, already imagining a calm, dry stall. The plumber meets you at the access hatch and assures you the leak is under control. Unfortunately, he adds, the lavatories cannot flush without water.

You tell yourself that this is an inconvenience you can reason with. Then you hear the porters outside counting toilets.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_isolator_entire.text:
You heave the MAIN lever downward. Every water pipe in the building gives a long, theatrical sigh. The flood behind you stops.

An instant later, somewhere in the ballroom, a fountain sputters to a halt. There is a collective gasp, followed by a loud voice announcing that the champagne is not included in the plumbing contract.

You have rescued the restroom at the expense of every tap in the Grand Bellevue. On the bright side, nobody can accuse you of doing things by halves.

The groom, if he is still hiding nearby, makes no attempt to congratulate you.

choices.text: HEAD TOWARD THE WEDDING TO EXPLAIN THE WATER SHUTOFF.
TAKE THE SERVICE STAIRS TO THE LOADING DOCK.

hotel_stall_lot_claimed.text:
You slip into the nearest stall and pull the door closed.

It even latches.

For one glorious moment, you are alone in a bathroom. An ordinary bathroom. With an actual toilet.

You reach toward your belt.

CLANK.

Something shifts overhead. Four steel cables pull taut around the stall's partitions. The walls tremble. Then, with a deep mechanical groan, the entire enclosure begins rising.

You look up. A crane is lifting the stall—walls, door, latch and all—straight through an open service hatch in the ceiling.

You remain exactly where you are. Standing beside the toilet. Fully dressed. Your hand is still hovering halfway toward your belt buckle.

Through the restroom entrance, whose doors were removed only moments earlier, you find yourself facing a small procession of wedding guests. They stop. You stop. The stall continues upward.

A porter checks his clipboard, looks at you, and gives an apologetic little wave.

You slowly lower your hand. The toilet is still there. Unfortunately, everyone can see it. And you.

choices.text: EXCUSE ME! I'M USING THAT!
JUMP AND GRAB THE RISING STALL BEFORE IT DISAPPEARS.
WALK PAST THE WEDDING GUESTS AS THOUGH NOTHING UNUSUAL HAS HAPPENED.

hotel_maintenance_dock_exit.text:
The iron stairway rattles under your feet. A swinging door at the bottom opens onto the hotel's loading dock. Crates, furniture, and a grand piano occupy most of the floor. An elaborate wedding cake is being wheeled dangerously close to the freight elevator.

You are still looking for the staff restroom sign when a foreman spots you and points sharply at the moving equipment.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_wheel_buyer_lead.speaker: hotel_plumber_assistant
text: Oh, I remember him. Green auction paddle. Little cap with an anchor on it.

text.say: Where did he go?

text: Toward the wedding drinks, I think. Said he was going to turn an ice bucket into a boat.

text.desc: Eddie retrieves a damp receipt from his pocket. The ink is beginning to spread.

text: Twelve for the lot. Seemed a fair price.

text.say: It's the emergency water shutoff, Eddie.

text: Well, he did ask if it worked under pressure.

choices.text: FIND THE BUYER WITH THE GREEN PADDLE.
EXAMINE EDDIE'S RECEIPT FOR THE LOT NUMBER.
LEAVE THE AUCTION ALONE AND TRY THE MAINTENANCE SHUTOFF.

hotel_lot_receipt_study.text:
The little receipt is almost illegible. You smooth it against a dry patch of tile.

LOT 14 — BRASS WATER SHUTOFF WHEEL.
BUYER — COMMODORE E. BIXBY.
PURCHASE PRICE — 12.00.
DECLARED PURPOSE — NAVAL DECORATION.

At the bottom, someone has stamped ALL SALES FINAL, including the emergency fixtures. There is a small handwritten exception: UNLESS THE BRIDE OBJECTS.

choices.text: FIND COMMODORE BIXBY AND ASK FOR THE WHEEL.
TAKE THE LOT NUMBER TO THE AUCTIONEER AND CHALLENGE THE SALE.

hotel_commodore_bixby.speaker: hotel_commodore_bixby

text.desc: At the edge of the reception, a gentleman in a miniature naval cap has mounted the stolen valve wheel on a silver ice bucket. A green auction paddle sticks out of his coat pocket.

text: There she is! Fine little craft, isn't she?

text.desc: He gives the wheel an experimental turn. The bucket rolls into a chair. He catches it just before it falls.

text: Rudder needs work, but we'll have her seaworthy by Thursday.

text.desc: Water creeps out from beneath the ballroom door and touches the toe of his polished shoe. He looks down with professional interest.

text: Tide's coming in.

choices.text: THAT'S THE HOTEL'S SHUTOFF WHEEL. THE BUILDING IS FLOODING!
TRADE YOUR RUBBER BAND BALL AS A FENDER FOR HIS LITTLE BOAT.
GO BACK TO THE AUCTIONEER AND DEMAND THE SALE BE REVERSED.

hotel_bixby_emergency.speaker: hotel_commodore_bixby

text.desc: The Commodore straightens so abruptly that his tiny cap nearly falls off.

text: An emergency at sea! Why didn't you say so?

text.desc: He pulls the wheel free of the ice bucket and presses it into your hands.

text: Take the helm, sailor. Save the vessel. I'll be expecting a tour of the bridge when this is all over.

text.desc: Behind him, a wedding guest slips on the advancing water. The Commodore blows a small whistle and begins organizing a lifeboat drill using dining chairs.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_bixby_trade.speaker: hotel_commodore_bixby

text.desc: You offer the rubber band ball. It is almost exactly the right size for the ice bucket. Bixby sets it alongside his little vessel and gasps.

text: A perfect fender! Look at the elasticity!

text.desc: He hands you the brass wheel without another word, then ties the rubber band ball to the bucket with a length of napkin. It remains with him, part of his new ship.

text: Splendid trade, sailor. Safe passage!

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_wheel_return.text:
You hurry back through the lobby carrying the brass wheel. A small river has formed across the marble floor. The plumber sees you, seizes the wheel, and fits it onto the bare valve shaft.

One turn. A second. The roaring water dies away. Eddie gives a relieved little clap.

The plumber tells you that you have saved the hotel an enormous repair bill. Unfortunately, the water is shut off until the pipes can be repaired. There will be no flushing for a while.

You glance toward the stalls. You feel a small, unreasonable hope.

There is a scraping sound from the other end of the room.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_key_master_cabinet.text:
The Facilities Key slides into the emergency cabinet as if it has been waiting there for you. One quarter turn, and the catch opens.

Inside is a single large red lever. You pull it. The pipes shudder, the water subsides, and the room becomes suddenly quiet.

The plumber peers at the key's paper tag. The return date says today, four fifty-two, and the signature belongs to the examiner.

He looks at you. Then at the signature. Then back at you. In the end he chooses to be grateful rather than curious.

You keep the key. The line is shut off, but the last stall is still standing. For now.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_stall_porter_protest.speaker: hotel_porter

text.desc: The porter looks down from his clipboard.

text: Of course you are, sir. That's why we left you there.

text.desc: You point toward the stall, now halfway through the ceiling.

text: We're strictly prohibited from lifting occupied fixtures. So we've removed the fixture and left the occupant. Perfectly safe.

text.desc: He makes a checkmark on the clipboard.

text: Now, if you're disputing the sale, that's an entirely different matter.

text.desc: You attempt to explain that you simply want to use the toilet. The porter produces a bright red placard.

text: Oh, you must take that up with the auctioneer. Here, I'll signal him.

text.desc: He waves the placard enthusiastically.

text: DISPUTE ON LOT FIFTY-THREE!

text.say: An objection? Excellent! Competitive interest! Bring the gentleman forward!

text.desc: A wedding guest applauds. The porter ushers you into the lobby toward the podium.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_auction_reopen_53.speaker: hotel_auctioneer

text.desc: The porter ushers you toward the podium. The elderly gentleman in the crimson dinner jacket looks delighted.

text: Ah! Our dissatisfied gentleman! Welcome, welcome!

text.desc: He taps his gavel.

text: Ladies and gentlemen! An unexpected development! Lot Fifty-Three has attracted additional interest!

text.say: Papa, you've already sold Lot Fifty-Three!

text: Indeed, darling. And now we have an opportunity to sell it again.

text.say: You can't sell the same toilets twice!

text: My dear, there are three of them.
And here we have a gentleman who has personally inspected the merchandise!

text.desc: You attempt to explain that you have no intention of purchasing a toilet.

text: Naturally! A discerning customer! Quite right to examine one's investment before committing!

text.say: Papa! He's trying to use the bathroom!

text: Then he understands its value better than anyone in the room!

text.desc: A wedding guest raises a paddle, followed by another.

text: Twenty-five! Thirty! Thirty from the lady by the flowers!

text.desc: The bride looks horrified. The auctioneer raises his gavel.

text: Thirty going once—

choices.text: I'M NOT BIDDING! I JUST WANT TO USE THE TOILET!
MISS, CAN'T YOU MAKE YOUR FATHER STOP SELLING EVERYTHING?
I WANT A WRITTEN RECORD OF MY OBJECTION!

hotel_auction_testimonial.speaker: hotel_auctioneer

text.desc: The auctioneer's eyes light up.

text: A testimonial! Ladies and gentlemen, our exceptional water pressure, personally verified by this gentleman!

text.desc: A wedding guest raises her hand.

text.say: Excuse me. Is it self-cleaning?

text: Madam, it washed this gentleman and half the corridor without anyone touching a single control!

text.say: Papa, that's a burst pipe!

text: Precisely! Fully automatic!

text.desc: The guest nods appreciatively. The auctioneer turns toward his clerk.

text: Make a note of our enthusiastic demonstrator!

text.desc: The clerk writes PRODUCT DEMONSTRATOR — GENTLEMAN, DAMP. You stare at the entry.

text: Splendid! Moving along!

text.desc: He raises his gavel.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_auction_bride_ally.speaker: hotel_bride

text.desc: The bride looks at you with sudden appreciation.

text: Believe me, I've been trying.
Papa can't remove anything without my signature in the blue delivery ledger. It's in his own contract.

text.say: A charming little formality.

text: It's at the loading dock. If you need to stop something being taken away, that's the paperwork.

text.say: A less charming formality.

text.desc: You now know where to challenge a removal. Nobody has asked you to fix the wedding.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_auction_dispute_ticket.speaker: hotel_auction_clerk

text.desc: The auctioneer looks delighted.

text.say: Certainly! Nothing inspires confidence quite like a dissatisfied customer!
See that the gentleman receives the appropriate paperwork.

text.desc: The clerk produces a small pad of red carbon-copy tickets.

text: Lot Fifty-Three. Formal objection. Reason for dispute?

text.desc: You point toward the ceiling, where the last corner of your former stall is disappearing. The clerk looks up.

text: Lack of privacy. Very good.

text.desc: He writes something, stamps the ticket, and tears off the top copy.

text: This entitles you to inspect the disputed merchandise before it leaves the hotel. Present it to the collection foreman.

text.say: A complimentary inspection! You see, sir? We take customer satisfaction very seriously!

text: It doesn't cancel the sale, mind you.

text.say: Naturally! We take sales even more seriously!

text.desc: The clerk hands you the ticket. The auctioneer returns to his gavel.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_auction_chair_lot31.speaker: hotel_auctioneer

text.desc: The auctioneer brings down his gavel.

text: SOLD! Lot Fifty-Three, to the lady in violet! May she enjoy her purchase in excellent health!

text.desc: The bride opens her mouth to protest, but two porters wheel an enormous high-backed upholstered chair toward the podium. A paper tag hangs from one leg: LOT 31 — BRIDAL SUITE CHAIR.

text: Moving along! Lot Thirty-One! A magnificent ceremonial chair, lovingly upholstered and barely used!

text.say: Wait. That's the chair he was carrying!

text: Who, darling?

text.say: The groom! Just before he disappeared!

text: Well, I'm delighted to report that at least the chair has turned up.

text.desc: One porter lifts the chair's front legs onto the display platform. The chair tilts. A faint metallic clink comes from the upholstery. You catch a brief flash of silver disappearing between cushion and wooden armrest. Neither the bride nor her father notices.

text: An exceptional piece! Fine craftsmanship! A fascinating history! Shall we open at fifteen?

text.desc: Guests begin examining their auction paddles. The bride keeps staring at the chair. You look toward the narrow gap where something disappeared.

choices.text: EXAMINE THE FLASH OF SILVER BETWEEN THE CHAIR CUSHIONS.
FOLLOW THE PORTERS WHEN THEY TAKE THE CHAIR TO THE COLLECTION AREA.

acting_director_badge.say: SHOW YOUR VEGETATION CREDENTIAL AND REQUEST AN INSPECTION OF THE CHAIR'S WOODEN FRAME.

expo_examiner_badge.say: SHOW YOUR EXAMINER BADGE AND DEMAND A PRE-SALE INSPECTION.

pavilion_temporary_staff_pass.say: SHOW YOUR STAFF PASS AND OFFER TO INSPECT LOT THIRTY-ONE BEFORE DELIVERY.

red_stapler.say: USE THE RED STAPLER TO PRY OPEN THE CHAIR'S UPHOLSTERY SEAM.

hotel_chair_vegetation_inspection.speaker: hotel_porter

text.desc: You present your Acting Director of Vegetation credential to the porter. He examines it carefully.

text: Vegetation?

text.desc: You gesture toward the chair's carved wooden arms. The porter looks at the chair, then your credential.

text: Well, I suppose it was a tree.

text.say: Quite right! We mustn't interfere with an official botanical inspection!

text.desc: The porter steps aside.

text: Very good, sir. Inspect away.

text.say: Ladies and gentlemen! Lot Thirty-One is now undergoing a government inspection! A valuable endorsement indeed!

text.desc: You approach the chair. The loose upholstery is within reach.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_chair_examiner_inspection.speaker: hotel_auction_clerk

text.desc: You present your Temporary Examiner Badge. The clerk examines it.

text: Office of Unverified Conditions. Is there something unverified about this item?

text.say: Certainly not! It's an excellent chair! Four legs, splendid upholstery, perfectly chair-shaped!

text: That's not quite the same as verifying its condition, sir.

text.desc: The clerk stamps the auction sheet: INSPECTION PENDING.

text.say: Pending? We're in the middle of bidding!

text: I'm afraid the sale must be suspended until the examiner has finished.

text.say: Ladies and gentlemen! A brief intermission while our magnificent chair undergoes an entirely unnecessary official inspection!

text.desc: He sets down his gavel. You approach the chair.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_chair_stapler_stealth.text:
The auctioneer launches into an enthusiastic description of the chair's craftsmanship. Everyone turns toward the podium.

You seize the opportunity. You slip behind the chair, wedge the stapler's metal base beneath the loosened upholstery, and carefully apply pressure.

Click.

The seam separates just enough. Something silver glints inside.

You withdraw the stapler, slip it into your pocket, and straighten up. The auctioneer is still talking. The porter is still watching the bidders. Nobody has noticed a thing.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_chair_stapler_caught.speaker: hotel_porter

text.desc: You wedge the stapler beneath the upholstered armrest. RRRIP. The stitching tears.

text: Sir! You've damaged the merchandise!

text.say: Good heavens! Is that your chair?

text.desc: You shake your head.

text.say: Well, it may very shortly have to be!
Papa, he hasn't purchased anything!
Then I suggest we find him a buyer before he damages anything else!

text.desc: You retrieve your stapler. The chair's upholstery is open, but everyone has noticed.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_chair_staff_escort.speaker: hotel_porter

text.desc: You present your Temporary Staff Pass to a porter. He examines it.

text: People's Pavilion? Isn't that the building across the courtyard?

text.desc: You point to the authorization for a service inspection. The porter reads it again.

text: One service inspection. Doesn't say what sort.

text.say: Ah! A visiting professional! Our merchandise attracts experts from across the Exposition!

text: Well, I suppose you can accompany the chair to collection. We're taking it down to the loading dock. Just stay clear of the freight equipment.

text.desc: He hands your pass back, considers the enormous chair, and looks at you.

text: Actually, since you're staff... mind giving us a hand?

text.desc: He hands you one end of a carrying strap. You find yourself helping two porters move Lot Thirty-One toward the service entrance.

text.say: Excellent initiative! That's the kind of service we pride ourselves on!

text.desc: You have become an employee of yet another establishment without applying for a job.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_chair_ring_focus.text:
The carved wooden arm of Lot Thirty-One fills your view.

A row of small brass tacks secures the dark red upholstery to the frame. One tack has worked loose.

Just beyond it, something silver catches the light.

You lean closer.

A ring.

A short length of pale blue ribbon is tangled around the band, trapping it between the wooden frame and a fold of fabric. Tiny letters are engraved along the inside, but you cannot make them out from this angle.

The ring is caught firmly enough that it won't simply fall out.

The chair shifts slightly as one of the porters adjusts its position. The ring slips a fraction deeper into the upholstery.

You need to decide what to do before the chair is taken away.

choices.text: WORK THE BLUE RIBBON LOOSE AND SLIP THE RING INTO YOUR POCKET.
WORK THE BLUE RIBBON LOOSE AND SLIP THE RING INTO YOUR POCKET.
LET THE PORTERS TAKE THE CHAIR, THEN FOLLOW IT TO COLLECTION.

hotel_ring_retrieved.text:
You pinch the pale blue ribbon between two fingers. Carefully, you work it backward through the loose stitching.

The ring shifts. You ease it along the wooden frame, trying not to snag the fabric.

For one dreadful moment, it hangs over the narrow gap.

Then it drops into your palm.

You close your fingers around it. A small silver wedding band rests against your skin. Tiny letters circle the inside, but they're too small to read here.

You slip the ring into your pocket before the chair can be moved.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_ring_slips.text:
You catch the ribbon between your fingers. It seems loose enough. You give it a careful tug.

Ping.

The brass upholstery tack snaps free. The ring slips from the ribbon, strikes the wooden frame, and disappears into the narrow cavity beneath the armrest.

You hear it rattle downward. Then silence.

You try to reach into the gap, but your fingers cannot get past the chair's internal supports. Before you can attempt anything else, the porters begin moving the chair.

One porter calls to the other to watch the arms. The buyer wants the chair in its original condition.

The chair is lifted onto its trolley. Somewhere inside the upholstery, the wedding ring is still rattling.

You watch Lot Thirty-One roll toward the collection entrance. The ring isn't lost forever, but you're going to have to follow the chair to retrieve it.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_stall_crane_success.text:
You catch the rising stall's metal frame with both hands.

Your feet leave the floor.

For one dreadful moment, you swing beneath the crane.

Then you find a foothold.

The stall rises toward an opening in the ceiling.

Below you, the restroom shrinks into the distance.

You have successfully escaped the bathroom.

Unfortunately, that's the exact opposite of what you wanted.

choices.text: CONTINUE

fatal_stall_final_occupancy.text:
Your fingers slip.

The stall continues upward.

You don't.

For one extraordinary moment, you have an uninterrupted view of the restroom below.

Including the toilet.

Directly below you.

You land on it.

There is a tremendous crack.

Then several smaller ones.

The toilet breaks.

So do you.

For the first and last time today, you have finally managed to use a toilet.

You would have preferred a less permanent arrangement.

ENDING — FINAL OCCUPANCY.

choices.text: BEGIN AGAIN

deathPopup.title: FINAL OCCUPANCY
deathPopup.description: The collection crew reports that Lot Fifty-Three has suffered considerable damage during removal. The associated toilet is declared beyond repair. Your restroom visit is recorded as COMPLETED. The auctioneer considers this an excellent example of customer satisfaction.

fatal_stall_final_occupancy.notes: Owner-approved fatal lead-in and popup copy. Planned aftermath illustration only: broken porcelain toilet beneath the raised empty stall, scattered auction tags, perhaps an abandoned shoe. Do not show the player's face; no death art generated yet. Engine popup uses the standard RETRY/CHECKPOINT/EXIT controls when integrated.

wip_stall_crane_ride.text: DRAFT REVIEW STOP — Survive the d6 grip check and ride the still-rising stall into upper salvage; choose the next way out without automatically finding a working toilet. This is not a gameplay ending.

wip_stall_wedding_walk.text: DRAFT REVIEW STOP — Unwritten result of walking past the wedding guests with dignity. This is not a gameplay ending.

text.desc: You trail Lot Thirty-One through the service door. The porters wheel it past empty shipping crates toward the collection stairs.
Nobody questions your presence. Apparently, following furniture around is perfectly normal here.
At every bump, something metallic rattles inside the upholstered armrest. The ring is still there.
The trolley rounds a corner. You keep pace.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_chair_staff_escort_loading.speaker: hotel_porter

text.desc: You carry one end of Lot Thirty-One through the service passage. The porter checks your Staff Pass again.

text: Doesn't say anything about furniture removal.

text.desc: He hands it back.

text: Doesn't say you can't, either.

text.desc: You continue carrying the chair. Your authorization has become remarkably physical.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_ring_in_pocket.text: You straighten beside Lot Thirty-One. A pale blue thread clings to your cuff. The wedding ring is safely in your pocket. Nearby, the bride argues with a porter about a chair. You still need a toilet.

choices.text: SHOW THE WEDDING RING TO THE BRIDE.
KEEP THE RING AND LOOK FOR ANOTHER RESTROOM.

hotel_ring_show_bride.speaker: hotel_bride

text.desc: You approach the bride and open your hand. The silver ring rests in your palm, with a bit of pale blue ribbon still caught around it.

text: Oh! That's the ring! That's the one he was supposed to bring!

text.desc: Her relief lasts about a second.

text: Where did you find it?

text.desc: You point toward Lot Thirty-One.

text: Of course. That miserable chair.

text.say: Ah! A charming matching accessory! Shall we start at—

text: Papa. No.

text.say: Withdrawn! Entirely withdrawn!

text.desc: The bride looks back at you. She doesn't take the ring yet.

text.say: Can I help you?

choices.text: PLACE THE RING IN THE BRIDE'S HAND.
I'M SORRY, BUT I STILL NEED A BATHROOM. CAN YOU HELP ME?

hotel_bride_ring_handover.speaker: hotel_bride

text.desc: You hold out the ring. The bride cups her hand beneath yours. The ring and its pale blue ribbon fall into her palm.

text: Oh.

text.desc: She turns it over.

text: Thank you. Truly.

text.say: A splendid private transaction! Shall we enter it as Lot Thirty-One A?

text: Papa, it isn't an auction lot!

text.say: Then a complimentary return! Excellent service!

text.desc: She closes her fingers around the ring.

text: You've brought back the one thing here I actually wanted.

text.desc: A pause.

text: Well. One of two things.

text.desc: She glances toward the service passage.

text: Listen. If you need to get through the staff corridors, tell the porters you're helping me. They should let you pass.
And if you find him... please tell him I just want him back.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_bride_ring_bathroom.speaker: hotel_bride

text.desc: The bride looks closely at you.

text: Oh! You're the gentleman they left standing beside the toilet!

text.say: The stall, miss. We removed the stall.

text: Yes, thank you.

text.desc: She considers this.

text: There is a private lavatory off the bridal dressing room upstairs. The wedding organizer has the key.
She's in the ballroom. Probably arguing with the musicians.

text.say: Magnificent acoustics in that room! Lot—

text: Papa.

text.say: I hadn't said a number!

text: And you won't.

text.desc: She points toward the public staircase.

text: Upstairs, left at the flowers. Find the organizer and tell her what happened.

text.desc: She lowers her voice.

text: And please don't let my father find out there's another bathroom.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_collection_stairs.text:
You reach the collection stairs.

The auctioneer's voice still carries through the ventilation grilles.

Two porters struggle to free Lot Thirty-One from a narrow doorway.

Beneath the trolley wheel lies a crushed white boutonnière and a delivery slip.

LOT 31 — BRIDAL SUITE CHAIR

ATTACHED GENTLEMAN — NOT INCLUDED

NOT INCLUDED has been underlined three times.

Beyond the chair, a door reads:

BOILER ACCESS — AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL ONLY

Something scrapes behind it.

A man coughs, then abruptly goes quiet.

You may have found the groom.

You also spot a sign pointing toward the staff lavatory.

A bright red SOLD sticker covers the arrow.

Naturally.

choices.text: EXCUSE ME. WHAT HAPPENED TO THE GENTLEMAN WHO CAME WITH THAT CHAIR?
SLIP THROUGH THE BOILER-ROOM DOOR WHILE THE PORTERS STRUGGLE WITH THE CHAIR.
SHOW YOUR TEMPORARY STAFF PASS AND REQUEST ACCESS TO THE MAINTENANCE AREA.
INVESTIGATE THE STAFF LAVATORY DESPITE THE SOLD SIGN.
INSPECT LOT THIRTY-ONE'S ARMREST BEFORE THE CHAIR IS CRATED.

text.desc: The porters pause with Lot Thirty-One tilted in the doorway. You crouch beside the armrest. A few loose brass tacks expose a narrow cavity beneath the red upholstery.
The wedding ring has fallen beneath a wooden brace. Now that the chair is tilted, you can see it, but your fingers cannot reach.
A silver wedding band is caught in a strand of pale blue ribbon behind the loosened fabric.
The porters stand close enough to help—and close enough to notice any tampering. The delivery manifest lists one chair. It does not list a wedding ring.

choices.text: ASK THE PORTER TO REMOVE THE UNLISTED WEDDING RING.
STOP INSPECTING AND RETURN TO THE COLLECTION STAIRS.

red_stapler.say: USE THE RED STAPLER TO OPEN THE UPHOLSTERY SEAM AND FREE THE RING.

hotel_collection_ring_focus.notes: Owner-approved Focus A. The Red Stapler action must be displayed locked with REQUIRES / NOT IN INVENTORY when absent in final gameplay UI. Do not repeat the earlier stapler stealth d6 at collection. The ring is not given until the player explicitly chooses a recovery method.

hotel_collection_ring_porter_recovery.speaker: hotel_porter

text.desc: You point to the silver ring lodged inside the armrest, then to the delivery manifest.

text.say: THAT RING ISN'T ON YOUR MANIFEST.

text: Then it isn't included in the sale.

text.say: Can you get it out?

text: We'd better. Imagine delivering something the buyer hasn't paid for.

text.desc: He carefully tilts the chair and pulls back the loose upholstery. The ring slides along the wooden frame. He catches it in his palm.

text.say: Should we list it as recovered?

text: No. It wasn't included.

text.desc: He hands you the ring.

text: Best take that before somebody puts a price on it.

text.desc: You slip the wedding ring into your pocket.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_collection_ring_stapler_recovery.speaker: hotel_porter

text.desc: The porters are bent over their delivery manifest. You slip the red stapler from your pocket.
Using its metal base, you carefully lever the loose upholstery away from the wooden armrest. The opening widens. You tilt the chair slightly.
The wedding ring rolls along the wooden frame and drops into your palm. Click.

text: If anything's fallen off, put it on the discrepancy form.

text.desc: You slip the stapler and ring into your pockets. No discrepancies are reported.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_collection_ring_stapler_recovery.notes: Owner-approved reliable item-assisted recovery without a second stealth check, with no new upholstery damage and no consumption of the Red Stapler.

hotel_collection_ring_in_pocket.text:
The silver ring is safely in your pocket. The porters return to their chair and the collection paperwork.

You can retrace the corridor to the bride, continue toward the boiler room where somebody coughed, or try the staff lavatory.

The ring can wait. Your bladder would prefer otherwise.

choices.text: RETURN TO THE BRIDE WITH THE WEDDING RING.
FOLLOW THE CLUE TOWARD BOILER THREE.
CHECK THE STAFF LAVATORY.

hotel_collection_ring_to_bride.text:
You retrace the service passage and emerge beside the auction floor. The bride is still watching the collection crews, looking increasingly concerned.

You approach with the ring.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_collection_porters_groom_clue.speaker: hotel_porter

text.desc: The porter looks at you, then consults his delivery slip.

text: Ah. The gentleman. Yes. There was a little misunderstanding.

text.say: We had him listed under accessories.

text: Until the auction clerk informed us that the groom wasn't included in the sale.

text.say: He was very relieved.

text.desc: The porter points toward the boiler-access door.

text: He went through there when he heard his future father-in-law calling.

text.desc: A metallic clang comes from behind the door. Both porters look toward it.

text.say: He's been doing that for ten minutes.

text: Every time the auctioneer shouts SOLD, he knocks something over.

text.desc: The porter returns his attention to the chair.

text: If you find him, please tell him he can't have the chair back. It's already been purchased.

text.desc: The second porter leans toward you.

text.say: And tell him we're sorry about the crate.

text.desc: The first porter gives him a warning look.

text: We agreed not to mention the crate.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_collection_slip_unnoticed.text:
You squeeze between Lot Thirty-One and the wall as both porters heave against the chair.

A loose strip of upholstery catches your sleeve.

The chair lurches sideways.

You're still attached.

You duck with the chair's movement, grab the boiler-room handle, and slip inside.

Behind you, the porters congratulate themselves on finally moving the chair.

They haven't.

The door clicks shut.

Neither porter notices your departure.

Warm pipes hiss overhead.

Around the nearest boiler, the hem of a wedding coat disappears from view.

You straighten your sleeve.

You appear to be considerably easier to transport than the furniture.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_collection_slip_spotted.speaker: hotel_porter

text.desc: You squeeze behind Lot Thirty-One as the porters shove. Your sleeve catches on the trim. The chair swings around. Unfortunately, so do you.
You find yourself face-to-face with a startled porter.

text: Sir! You're attached to the merchandise!

text.say: Is he included?

text.desc: The first porter examines his delivery slip.

text: Certainly not. It says so three times.

text.desc: He carefully detaches your sleeve from the chair, produces a small paper tag, and pins it to your coat: NOT INCLUDED.

text: There. That should prevent any further confusion.

text.desc: He opens the boiler-room door and ushers you through.

text: Please keep clear of the collection area, sir.

text.desc: The door closes behind you. You look down at your new label. Apparently, you're no longer considered merchandise. A small victory.
Beyond the nearest boiler, the hem of a wedding coat disappears behind the pipes.

choices.text: CONTINUE

text.desc: You produce your Temporary Staff Pass. The porter examines it, looks at Lot Thirty-One, and consults his clipboard.

choices.text: CONTINUE
CONTINUE

hotel_collection_staff_pass_first.speaker: hotel_porter
text: People's Pavilion? Isn't that across the courtyard?

text.say: It says temporary staff.

text: Yes, but temporary staff for whom?

text.desc: The second porter looks around at the half-dismantled hotel.

text.say: At this rate, all the staff are temporary.

text.desc: The first porter considers this.

text: Fair point.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_collection_staff_pass_recognized.speaker: hotel_porter
text: Oh! Our visiting inspector. Back again?

text.say: Excellent. Perhaps he can explain why this chair won't fit through the door.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_collection_staff_pass_authorized.speaker: hotel_porter

text.desc: The porter retrieves his clipboard.

text: Name?

text.desc: You gesture toward the pass. He writes TEMPORARY.

text: Purpose of visit?

text.desc: You indicate the boiler-room door. He writes OFFICIAL.
The porter steps aside and returns your pass.

text: Very good. Authorized maintenance inspection.
And if you happen to find a gentleman in wedding clothes back there, please tell him he isn't part of Lot Thirty-One.

text.say: We've checked twice.

text.desc: You enter the boiler passage. Apparently, you have been hired again.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_staff_lavatory_storage.speaker: hotel_wedding_assistant

text.desc: You push open the staff lavatory door. There is a toilet. An actual toilet. Unfortunately, it is buried beneath approximately three hundred boxes of wedding favors.
A young wedding assistant is balancing a stack of place cards on the cistern.

text: Oh! You're not here for the favors, are you?

text.desc: You point toward the toilet.

text: Oh. That.

text.desc: She looks embarrassed.

text: The auctioneer sold us this room as additional wedding storage.

text.desc: You look at the boxes.

text: He called it a convenience facility. Apparently, he didn't specify whose convenience.

text.desc: She adjusts a wobbling stack.

text: There's another lavatory off the bridal dressing room upstairs. But the wedding organizer has the key.
She's in the ballroom. Last I heard, she was threatening the violinists.

text.desc: The assistant places another box on the toilet.

text: Please don't move anything. I've finally got them arranged by table number.

choices.text: COULD YOU MOVE THESE BOXES? I REALLY NEED TO USE THAT TOILET.
FIND THE WEDDING ORGANIZER IN THE BALLROOM.
RETURN TO THE BOILER-ACCESS DOOR AND CONTINUE SEARCHING FOR THE GROOM.

hotel_staff_lavatory_move_boxes.speaker: hotel_wedding_assistant

text.desc: The assistant looks sympathetic.

text: Oh! Of course. Just a moment.

text.desc: She begins removing boxes. You help clear a space around the toilet. For the first time in what feels like hours, you can actually see the seat.

text: There! That should—

text.desc: She stops. A red ribbon is stretched across the toilet lid. Attached to it is an auction tag: LOT 58 — STAFF TOILET. SOLD — COLLECTION AFTER CEREMONY. DO NOT TEST.
The assistant stares at it.

text: Oh, dear.

text.desc: She reads the tag again.

text: He sold the room to us for storage and the toilet to somebody else.

text.desc: She looks genuinely embarrassed.

text: I'm terribly sorry. The buyer apparently insists on receiving it in its original condition.

text.desc: She carefully replaces one of the boxes.

text: I really think you should find the wedding organizer.

text.desc: You look at the toilet. It looks perfectly functional. That somehow makes everything worse.

choices.text: IGNORE THE AUCTION TAG AND TRY TO USE THE TOILET ANYWAY.
FIND THE WEDDING ORGANIZER IN THE BALLROOM.
RETURN TO THE BOILER ROOM AND CONTINUE SEARCHING FOR THE GROOM.

hotel_staff_lavatory_temporary_use_permi.speaker: hotel_wedding_assistant

text.desc: You remove the SOLD ribbon and lift the toilet lid. Finally. You reach toward your belt.

text: Wait! You'll need a Temporary Use Permit.

text.desc: She checks her clipboard.

text: To issue one, I first need to verify that the toilet flushes.

text.desc: You reach for the handle.

text: No! Testing a sold toilet requires a Temporary Use Permit!

text.desc: She looks at the paperwork.

text: Oh.

text.desc: A pause.

text: Well, there's an exception form. The wedding organizer can sign it.

text.desc: She places her clipboard on the toilet seat.

text: Shall I start the paperwork?

text.desc: You stare at the toilet. Two feet away. Completely functional. Entirely unavailable.

choices.text: YES. WHERE CAN I FIND THE WEDDING ORGANIZER?
LEAVE THE PAPERWORK BEHIND AND RETURN TO THE BOILER ROOM.

hotel_boiler_pressure_intro.speaker: hotel_boiler_engineer

text.desc: The boiler room is sweltering. A pressure gauge trembles in the red. Beside it stands a chained door marked ENGINEERS' LAVATORY.

text: Closed until we complete the emergency pressure test.

text.say: THERE'S A TOILET IN THERE?

text: Allegedly.

text.desc: He points toward a large brass wheel.

text: Regulations require an independent volunteer to operate that while I certify the results.

text.desc: The warning plate reads HIGH-PRESSURE STEAM. The engineer is standing remarkably far away.

text.say: AND THEN I CAN USE THE TOILET?

text: Then you can apply.

text.desc: Somebody coughs behind Boiler Three.

text: Gentleman in a wedding suit wouldn't volunteer either. Said he was under enough pressure already.

choices.text: VOLUNTEER TO OPERATE THE PRESSURE-RELIEF WHEEL.
SHOW THE LOT 53 DISPUTE TICKET AND DEMAND AN INSPECTION HOLD.
SHOW YOUR TEMPORARY STAFF PASS AND REQUEST MAINTENANCE ACCESS.
LOOK BEHIND BOILER THREE, AWAY FROM THE PRESSURE WHEEL.
LEAVE THE BOILER ROOM AND SEARCH THE SERVICE PASSAGE.

hotel_boiler_pressure_intro.notes: Owner-approved tightened boiler incident. Hidden d6: 1–4 fatal, 5–6 survive, no modifiers. Four cards remain visible in future engine presentation; B and C must be disabled with REQUIRES / NOT IN INVENTORY subtitles if their items are absent. The current review JSON uses if.has gating because the game engine cannot yet display locked missing-item cards. Do not replay the later groom introduction when ch4_groom_located is already true.

hotel_boiler_pressure_relieved.speaker: hotel_boiler_engineer

text.desc: You turn the wheel. Steam roars overhead. The gauge drops into the green.

text: PASS! Beautifully done!

text.desc: He unlocks the passage. Beyond it, another door reads SANITATION CLEARANCE PENDING.

text.say: YOU SAID IT WOULD OPEN!

text: The passage did. Excellent progress!

text.desc: A nervous cough comes from behind Boiler Three.

choices.text: CONTINUE

fatal_boiler_pressed_and_steamed.text:
You turn the wheel.

The valve shrieks.

An enormous cloud of steam engulfs you.

When it clears, your tuxedo hangs from a wire hanger. Jacket and trousers, perfectly pressed. Still steaming.

The engineer examines the result.

Well. At least the steam press works.

ENDING — PRESSED AND STEAMED.

choices.text: BEGIN AGAIN

deathPopup.title: PRESSED AND STEAMED
deathPopup.description: The emergency pressure test has passed. Your formalwear has never looked better. Unfortunately, its former occupant is unavailable for comment.

fatal_boiler_pressed_and_steamed.notes: Owner-approved fatal outcome with d6 1–4, no modifiers. Illustration ONLY: a steaming tuxedo jacket and matching trousers together on a single wire clothes hanger, as though freshly steam-pressed. Simple, immediately absurd visual. No boiler, gauge, clipboard, shoe, text, person, face, or gore in the artwork. No image generated yet. Popup has exactly one incident-specific heading and its narrative beside art; future engine has RETRY/CHECKPOINT/EXIT controls.

hotel_boiler_dispute_hold.speaker: hotel_boiler_engineer

text.desc: You show the red carbon-copy Lot 53 Dispute Ticket.

text: That's for a toilet stall.

text.desc: You point toward the connected pipes.

text: Oh, bother. Associated fixtures.

text.desc: He hangs a DO NOT OPERATE tag on the pressure-relief wheel.

text: Can't test disputed equipment. Safety regulations.

text.say: SO THE TOILET'S OPEN?

text: No test, no opening. Excellent safety record!

text.desc: He unchains the inspection walkway. Somebody coughs behind Boiler Three.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_boiler_dispute_hold.notes: Owner-approved item-bypass payoff. Lot 53 Dispute Ticket stays in inventory; safety test suspended rather than passed, lavatory remains closed.

hotel_boiler_staff_access.speaker: hotel_boiler_engineer

text.desc: You show your Temporary Staff Pass.

text.say: Ah, the temporary official the porters sent down. They warned me you were coming.
Temporary staff? Well, I suppose that's most of our staff these days.

text: Then you're ineligible to volunteer.

text.say: THAT'S GOOD.

text: For you. Terrible for our staffing plan.

text.desc: He opens the maintenance gate. From behind Boiler Three comes another cough.

choices.text: CONTINUE

hotel_boiler_staff_access.notes: Owner-approved Staff Pass bypass. Pass retained, no roll, boiler pressure remains high, lavatory stays closed. Conditional porter recognition is a brief callback and must not add another full conversation.

hotel_boiler_groom_encounter.speaker: hotel_groom

text.desc: You round Boiler Three. A man in a rumpled wedding suit crouches behind a stack of coal scuttles.

text.say: If you're here for the wedding, I'm not available.
I'M LOOKING FOR A TOILET.
Oh. Then you're having a worse day than I am.
SOLD!

text.desc: The groom ducks at the sound coming through the vent.

text.say: Apparently there's a private lavatory off the bridal dressing room. The organizer has the key.

text.desc: That's considerably more useful than anything else he's said.

choices.text: HOW DO I REACH THE BRIDAL DRESSING ROOM?
SHOW THE GROOM THE WEDDING RING.
LEAVE HIM HIDING AND RETURN TO THE SERVICE PASSAGE.

hotel_boiler_groom_encounter.notes: Owner-approved bladder-first replacement. Ring SHOW is visible but locked when item absent in future UI, with REQUIRES: WEDDING RING — LOT 31. No groom escort, wedding reunion, or persuasion check.

hotel_groom_show_ring.speaker: hotel_groom

text.desc: You show the silver band, its pale blue ribbon still attached.

text.say: The ring! You found it!
IN A CHAIR.
I tied that ribbon around it because I was afraid I'd lose it.
GOOD SYSTEM.
I see the flaw now. Better keep hold of it. I don't trust myself.
I WASN'T OFFERING.
AS IS, WHERE IS?
I thought it sounded romantic. Her father asked whether it was legally binding.

text.desc: You pocket the ring again.

choices.text: ASK HOW TO REACH THE BRIDAL LAVATORY.
LEAVE THE GROOM TO HIS HIDING PLACE.

hotel_groom_show_ring.notes: Ring remains in inventory; inscription joke only if inspected earlier. No handover or wedding task.

wip_bride_staff_corridor_route.text: DRAFT REVIEW STOP — Bride has the wedding ring; her support grants staff-corridor permission. Build the service passage follow-up without automatically locating the groom. This is not a gameplay ending.

wip_bride_find_wedding_organizer.text: DRAFT REVIEW STOP — Follow the upstairs flower direction to the wedding organizer for the private bridal-dressing-room lavatory key. No automatic bathroom access; account for any prior organizer meeting. Ring remains in inventory. This is not a gameplay ending.

hotel_lot61_pod_auction.speaker: hotel_auctioneer

text.desc: Back on the auction floor, a wedding guest raises her hand.

text.say: Excuse me. If you're selling all the bathrooms, where are we supposed to go?

text: An excellent question! Ladies and gentlemen, Lot Sixty-One!

text.desc: Two porters wheel out a gleaming metal booth.

text: The Grand Bellevue Emergency Convenience Pod! Completely self-contained! No plumbing required!

text.desc: The booth's door stands slightly open. Inside is a small porcelain toilet. An actual toilet.

text.say: Does it work?

text: Magnificently! Even during a complete hotel water outage!

text.say: Papa, why haven't we been using that?

text: Because, darling, we hadn't sold it yet!

text.desc: He turns toward the audience.

text: Who would care to demonstrate?

text.desc: His eyes settle on you.

text: Ah! Our gentleman with the urgent interest in modern conveniences!

text.desc: The porters open the booth's door. You can see a toilet, a seat, and what appears to be privacy.
A small warning plate beside the entrance reads: AUTOMATIC PACKING MECHANISM — DISENGAGE BEFORE OCCUPANCY. The auctioneer appears not to have noticed it.

choices.text: ENTER THE EMERGENCY CONVENIENCE POD AND TRY TO USE IT.
DECLINE THE DEMONSTRATION AND CONTINUE SEARCHING FOR THE GROOM.

hotel_lot61_pod_escaped.speaker: hotel_auctioneer

text.desc: You step inside. The door closes with a reassuring click. There is a toilet, walls, privacy. You are almost overcome with gratitude.
Outside, the auctioneer raises his voice.

text: Ladies and gentlemen! Observe the remarkable efficiency of our emergency sanitation system!

text.desc: You reach toward your belt.

text: And now, its most impressive feature!

text.desc: A mechanical clunk comes from beneath the floor.

text: Automatic packing for convenient transport!

text.desc: The walls begin moving inward. You grab the door handle. It won't turn.
You throw your weight against the door. The latch gives way. You tumble onto the auction floor.
Behind you, the booth folds inward with a series of metallic bangs. Seconds later, it has become a remarkably compact shipping case. The audience applauds.

text: Extraordinary! Completely portable!

text.desc: You stand up. Your clothing is intact. Your dignity is not. You still need a toilet.

choices.text: SEARCH THE SERVICE CORRIDORS FOR ANOTHER TOILET.

fatal_lot61_folded.text:
You step inside the Emergency Convenience Pod. The door closes with a reassuring click.

There is a toilet. There are walls. There is privacy.

You reach toward your belt.

Outside, the auctioneer announces the pod's most impressive feature: automatic packing for convenient transport.

A mechanical clunk comes from beneath the floor. The walls begin moving inward. You grab the door handle. It won't turn.

You pull desperately at the handle.

The walls keep closing.

The porcelain toilet disappears beneath a folding metal panel.

There is a final mechanical clunk.

Then silence.

Outside, the auctioneer beams at the audience.

And there we have it! Ready for immediate collection!

ENDING — FOLDED FOR CONVENIENCE.

choices.text: BEGIN AGAIN

deathPopup.title: FOLDED FOR CONVENIENCE
deathPopup.description: Lot Sixty-One has been successfully reduced to its transport dimensions. The collection crew reports that the unit is somewhat heavier than the manufacturer's specifications suggest. The auction clerk adds a note to the manifest: CONTENTS INCLUDED. No further inspection is deemed necessary.

fatal_lot61_folded.notes: Owner-approved fatal lead-in/popup copy and specific art brief. Future aftermath image must show a NORMAL-SIZED BRIEFCASE-SIZED folded metallic case or compact suit-like case, with only SLIGHT asymmetrical bulging to imply the body compressed inside and ONE loose shoe lying off to the side as if it fell out. No oversized packing container, exposed corpse, gore, or visible face. The ordinary case size is essential to the joke. No artwork generated yet. Engine popup uses standard RETRY/CHECKPOINT/EXIT controls when integrated. Hidden d6 roll is fatal on 1–4, escape on 5–6; no modifiers approved.

hotel_lot61_pod_declined.speaker: hotel_auctioneer

text.desc: The auctioneer looks disappointed.

text: A cautious gentleman! Quite right! Safety first!

text.desc: He turns toward the audience.

text: Who'll give me twenty-five?

text.desc: The porters begin wheeling the pod toward the collection area. You leave before anybody asks you to help.

choices.text: SEARCH THE SERVICE CORRIDORS FOR ANOTHER TOILET.

wip_ballroom_flood.text: DRAFT REVIEW STOP — Flood reaches the wedding corridor; the bride, cake, and guests react differently depending on water flags. This is not a gameplay ending.

wip_ballroom_water_off.text: DRAFT REVIEW STOP — The entire hotel loses water during the wedding. This is not a gameplay ending.

wip_auctioneer_dispute.text: DRAFT REVIEW STOP — Challenge the safety-equipment auction using the Lot 14 receipt or the buyer's testimony. This is not a gameplay ending.

text.say: HOW DO I GET TO THE BRIDAL DRESSING ROOM?
Service stairs. Up one floor, then left past the ballroom.
There's a door with white flowers around it. The wedding organizer has the key.
THANK YOU.
If you happen to see my bride, could you—
I'M LOOKING FOR A TOILET.
Right. Of course. Good luck.

text.desc: He ducks back into hiding. You take the service stairs toward the bridal corridor.

choices.text: CONTINUE

text.desc: You step around Boiler Three toward the service door.

text.say: You're not going to tell anyone I'm here, are you?
NO.
Thank you.

text.desc: You open the door.

text.say: And if anybody asks—

text.desc: You let the door close. His problems remain on the other side.
Ahead: the staff lavatory, stairs toward the ballroom, and a loading dock opening onto daylight. Still no toilet.

choices.text: CHECK THE STAFF LAVATORY.
TAKE THE SERVICE STAIRS TOWARD THE BALLROOM.
HEAD THROUGH THE LOADING DOCK AND LEAVE THE HOTEL.

text: You follow the service passage to the loading dock. Workers are still carrying pieces of the Grand Bellevue onto trucks. You pass the crates and approach a narrow pedestrian gate.

text.say: Leaving?
YES.
Use the side gate. It's the one thing they're not shipping.

text: You push through. Across the courtyard is a small public park: trees, grass, a few promising shrubs. Surely you can find a little privacy there.

You cross the courtyard and head toward the park.

END CHAPTER 4.
hotel_service_park_exit.notes: Owner-approved nonfatal Chapter 4 ending. Retain all inventory and existing fee flags, including ch4_bridal_registration_fee_pending if set. Chapter 5 introduces any fried animals, hidden security plant prototypes, or hazards; reveal none here. No bathroom sign.

hotel_boiler_service_passage.text: You leave the overheated boiler room. The service passage branches toward a staff lavatory, stairs to the ballroom, and a loading dock where daylight filters around stacked crates. Your bladder votes for whichever route has an actual working toilet.

choices.text: CHECK THE STAFF LAVATORY.
TAKE THE STAIRS TOWARD THE BRIDAL CORRIDOR.
LEAVE BY THE LOADING DOCK.
